Best,
Tareef

messages.subject: Change locale for shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
I've got a script which grabs a few datapoints from an API, does some data massaging, and then graphs it with ggplot. It works perfectly locally, but it fails on shinyapps because the locale is forced to be "C" and not "en_US." I've tried to set the locale to something else, but apparently (see snippet below) my only options are "C" or "POSIX."

    locales <- system("locale -a", intern = TRUE)
    library(stringr)
    print(unique(str_split_fixed(locales, "\\.", 2)[, 1]))

It might be avoidable in some circumstances, except that the API I'm working with returns dates like so: "Mon, 02 Mar 2015 05:15:00". The Month is only listed in the form of the abbreviation, %b in en_US.

Any suggestions on workarounds?

messages.subject: Re: Change locale for shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
The problem seems to go beyond just the locale.  It appears that the server running shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io> does not recognize month names (at least as input), and so it probably does not recognize month abbreviations, either (though I have not checked that).  See here <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28656683/r-script-working-locally-not-working-on-shinyapp-io> for more details.

My suggestion would be to change the string to reformat it as a numerical date, and reassemble it.  This page <https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-patched/library/base/html/strptime.html> gives an enormous list of date formats.  Yours appears to be "%a, %d %b %Y %X", but you want it to be "%d %m %Y %X".  I would be to use str_replace from the stringr package <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/stringr/stringr.pdf>.  Replace everything like "Mon, " with nothing, and replace everything like "Mar" with the relevant month number.  This will probably require 19 separate str_replace statements (one for each month and each day of the week).  Also, str_replace only works on one string at a time, but you can probably get around that using Vectorize <https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Vectorize.html>.

thank you Andy, I think i figured out what's wrong.

I put the install.packages only after using the code below failed, so I thought I needed to tell the server to install. Turns out the lapply + required trick is what was failing me. I need to call each package one by one with "library" in order for shinyapps to fetch them.

 libs <- c('lme4','car','MASS', 'scales', 'mixtools','arm','plyr', 'ggparallel','RColorBrewer', 'vegan','grid','gridExtra', 'sjPlot', 'MuMIn')
 lapply(libs, require, character.only = T)

messages.subject: verdana fonts not available
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to deploy an application on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, this application generate pptx thanks to ReporteRs package.

However, while my application runs on my machine (PC/Windows) it fails when I deploy it on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. It seems to come from the unavailability of some fonts. Indeed, in some ReporteRs function call, I use two classical fonts (Verdana and Century Gothic) which are available on my machine but not available on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

To check that I run
library(sysfonts)
font.files()

both on my machine and on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>
On my machine I get 497 fonts, including Verdana for instance
AGENCYB.TTF AGENCYR.TTF [...] CENTURY.TTF CHILLER.TTF [...] verdana.ttf verdanab.ttf verdanai.ttf verdanaz.ttf [...] WINGDNG3.TTF

On  shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> I get only 6 fonts :
DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf DejaVuSans.ttf DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf DejaVuSansMono.ttf DejaVuSerif-Bold.ttf DejaVuSerif.ttf

So my question is, how can I add some (classical) fonts on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> ?

Thanks!
Dom

messages.subject: Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
messages.subject_clean: Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm attempting to set up a simple remote application using shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but have hit a bit of a snag. What I'm looking to do is create a very simple survey which can be remotely deployed, but uses the local shiny interface defined by the mirtCAT package wrapper function (install.packages('mirtCAT')). E.g., locally, this works fine:

```{r}
library(mirtCAT)
options <- matrix(c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"),
                  nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
df <- data.frame(Question = c('Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3'), Option = options, Type = "radio")

## Run the mirtCAT web interface and store results
results <- mirtCAT(df = df)
```

Using some variant of this, I created a single executable source file called 'app.R', and uploaded it to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> location (http://philchalmers.shinyapps.io/mirtCAT-shinyapp_io). The problem is that, because mirtCAT calls shiny::runApp() internally and does a lot of pre and post processing, everything really needs to be deployed using a single R script (not a separate server.R and ui.R file).

After uploading the app.R file, I simply get the following: 'ERROR: Key / already in use', which likely is what is expected given my approach. Any tips or tricks to tell shinyapps to just source the app.R file and trust that runApp() is run internally would be greatly appreciated. Cheers.

Phil

Brgds,

Uwe

Here is the link that helps answer the question: http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/shinyapps-iobeta/

Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil, it looks like you're the author of this package?

I'd refactor the mirtCAT function to pull everything up to the runApp() into a separate function--let's call it createShinyApp. Then change the runApp() call to a shinyApp() call (so the createShinyApp function returns the result of shinyApp()).

Back in mirtCAT, you can call runApp(createShinyApp(...), launch.browser=TRUE) like you were before.

Your app.R on the other hand can call createShinyApp(...) as the last line in the file and that should work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

On Wed, Mar 4, 2015 at 4:28 PM, Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi all,
>
> I'm attempting to set up a simple remote application using shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but have hit a bit of a snag. What I'm looking to do is create a very simple survey which can be remotely deployed, but uses the local shiny interface defined by the mirtCAT package wrapper function (install.packages('mirtCAT')). E.g., locally, this works fine:
>
> ```{r}
> library(mirtCAT)
> options <- matrix(c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"),
>                   nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
> df <- data.frame(Question = c('Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3'), Option = options, Type = "radio")
>
> ## Run the mirtCAT web interface and store results
> results <- mirtCAT(df = df)
> ```
>
> Using some variant of this, I created a single executable source file called 'app.R', and uploaded it to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> location (http://philchalmers.shinyapps.io/mirtCAT-shinyapp_io). The problem is that, because mirtCAT calls shiny::runApp() internally and does a lot of pre and post processing, everything really needs to be deployed using a single R script (not a separate server.R and ui.R file).
>
> After uploading the app.R file, I simply get the following: 'ERROR: Key / already in use', which likely is what is expected given my approach. Any tips or tricks to tell shinyapps to just source the app.R file and trust that runApp() is run internally would be greatly appreciated. Cheers.
>
> Phil

messages.body_plain:
The other thing you should consider is adjusting the "Worker Startup Timeout" setting. This can be found under the "Advanced" tab on the Settings Page for your application in the dashboard.

I think what may be happening here is that if you are loading or processing a lot of data when the application starts up, you may be hitting the default startup time of 60 seconds. Increasing the "Worker Startup Timeout", may address this. However, it should be noted, that I would recommended examining your code to see if you can decrease your startup time, as you may experience poor performance by trying to operate on such a large data set.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Application failing to start
messages.body_plain:
I would say generally it depends. But as a general rule less data is better. shiny applications are designed to be interactive, and the more data processing that occurs slows down the responsiveness of the application, and can result in a poor user experience.

To reduce startup time, you could look at pre-processing data and saving it as RData files to be loaded by your application at startup.

On Sunday, February 1, 2015 at 11:41:40 PM UTC+8, Phill Clarke wrote:
> I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
>
> The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
>
> library("RMySQL")
>
> con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
>
> sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
>
> results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
>
> dbDisconnect(con)
>
> The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.
>
> If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.
>
> I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
>
> system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
>
> I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
>
> I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
>
> I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
>
> However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
>
> Error in .local(drv, ...) :
>   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
>
> Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
>
> If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
>
> I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
>
>
>
>

If I have an application that uses, say, a csv file as the source data, the application deploys fine with that data. What if I want the application to use a new version of the data in an updated csv file from my local server? Is there a way to upload that csv without having to manually deploy the application again? Can I do something equivalent to sftp to the shinyapps server? Or can I automate the deployment of the app (which would include the latest data file) from the local server each time I want a new version of the data to be available?
Thanks,
KJ

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Automatically Refreshing Source Data
messages.body_plain:
You have two options here. You should be able to deploy the application from the command line through R CMD with the shinyapps package.
The other option would be to have a mechanism in your application which downloads a new CSV from a web accessible location on startup of the application.  That would obviously be inefficient if the CSV file is large.

messages.subject: Re: after new r release shiny account needs payment
messages.subject_clean: after new r release shiny account needs payment
messages.body_plain:
Yoni,

You should have received email from RStudio regarding shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>'s end of beta testing period (March 6th). After this date you either need to upgrade your account to a paid plan for extra features, or stick with the free plan which has limited functionalities. Please refer to http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/ for list of plans and differences.

In your case it seems that you have crossed the max limits of free plan. You could have more than 5 active applications, or you have a private (authorized) application, or some other limitation of free plan.

I have CCed shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> forum on this email, but in future you can post to that discussion group for faster response:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shinyapps-users

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject_clean: Some but not all SVGs don't show up in a shinapps.io that are fine locally (solved - Windows v Linux problem)
messages.body_plain:
I resolved this problem myself in the process of writing this but decided to post anyway in case a similar problem happens for others.

I have an app under development that has lots of pre-prepared .svg files sitting in a folder ie www/images/*.svg.

In server.R they are created with text like
output$Triangle1 <- renderText("<object type='image/svg+xml' data='images/triangle1.svg'>")

And in ui.R they are pushed to the screen with:

htmlOutput("Triangle1"))

(Real example is dynamically created and more complex of course and there are other things going on with ggvis and stuff, but I get the same result even in a greatly cut down version with no graphics other than five hard coded svg calls like the above.)

This works perfectly locally on Windows.  When I push it to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> some of the SVGs showed up and some didn't.  Alert readers may have guessed why - careless capitalisation in the filenames.  Windows thinks triangle1.svg and Triangle1.svg are the same so it doesn't matter if the <object> tag gets it right or not; linux (rightly in my view) does care.

Look at these examples:

output$thePlot  <- renderPlot({
   plot(x,y)
})

or

})

so the 2nd method with the print works.  the first method without the print kind of works, but hangs or with a very slow time to do the plot.

In your code, is getPlot doing?  I thought that function was for extracting a plot from a plot matrix, but you have way too many parameters for that.

I made a small example based on what has been posted here.  In this example, there is no timing difference in the display of the two graphs.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Very slow ggplot
messages.body_plain:
So things get complicated when I post code, but I will give it a try

So here is the server code:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

pinByStrikes <- reactive({input$pinByStrikes})

graphType <- reactive({input$graphType})

stockText <- reactive({toupper(input$stock)})

expText <- reactive({input$yymmdd})

strikes <- reactive({input$strikes})

smoothOn <- reactive({input$smoothOn})

 withProgress(message = 'waiting for data', value = 0, {

lastQuote <- reactive({getQuote(stockText())$Last})

incProgress(0.2, detail = "got quote")

chain <- reactive({getYahooDataReformatted(stockText(), expText())})

incProgress(0.4, detail = "got options")

output$caption <- renderText({paste(stockText(), " $", lastQuote(), " Expiration ", expText())})

output$subCaption <- reactive({wasUpdatedToday(stockText(),chain(),expText())})

if (!is.null(chain)) reactive({cat("good option chain ", stockText(), expText(), "\n")})

incProgress(0.8, detail = "ready to plot")

})

output$openIntPlot <- renderPlot({

withProgress(message = 'waiting for plot', value = 0, {

    if (!is.null(chain()))

     p <- getPlot(graphType(),chain(), stockText(), strikes(), lastQuote(), smoothOn(), pinByStrikes())

else

plotError("No Data.  Either wrong date for this stock, or no prior data")

if (doProgress) incProgress(0.9, detail = "outputting plot")

print(p)

})

})

})

Again when I remove the print(p) and just do the getPlot without the assignment is when I feel I get the problem.  The hang occurs after the last incProgress(0.9, detail = "outputting plot"), so I was thinking it didn't matter what getPlot did, as that code ran fine.  getPlot basically just figures out which plot to generate, sets up some parameters, and returns the ggplot.  For the default the ggplot will be this:

p <- ggplot(openInt, aes(x=strike))

    + geom_area(aes(y = putOI,  fill = "1 put", colour = "1 put",   stat = "bin"), alpha = 0.5)

+ geom_area(aes(y = callOI, fill = "2 call",colour = "2 call",  stat = "bin"), alpha = 0.5)

+ geom_point(aes(y=callOI), size=1.5, alpha=.5, color="blue")

+ geom_point(aes(y=putOI),  size=1.5, alpha=.5, color="red")

+ scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty(sp$lower:sp$upper, n = theN))

    + theme(legend.title = element_blank())

    + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90,size=theSize))

    + theme(panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

I can post all the code if you want.  Or I can take out the print and redeploy the code.  If there was some way of debugging what was happening during the hang this might be useful.

Thanks

David

messages.subject: Re: Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.subject_clean: Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
Yes, unfortunately, my solution worked locally, but not when deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. On reflection, I am assuming this is because one can't launch an SSH session from a shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> hosted account. Next step is to try adding the IP addresses as suggested by Chad.

On Friday, 6 March 2015 01:52:49 UTC, THIAM HUAT Tan wrote:
> I need the same solution as what you encountered...
> but when I type what you suggested, it has error as below:
>
> > system(paste("sshpass -p 'remotesyspassword' ssh -f -L 3306:localhost:3306 username@remotsystemhostname sleep 20"))
> Warning message:
> running command 'sshpass -p 'remotesyspassword' ssh -f -L 3306:localhost:3306 username@remotsystemhostname sleep 20' had status 127
>
>
> On Sunday, February 1, 2015 at 11:41:40 PM UTC+8, Phill Clarke wrote:
> > I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
> >
> > The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
> >
> > library("RMySQL")
> >
> > con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
> >
> > sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
> >
> > results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
> >
> > dbDisconnect(con)
> >
> > The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.
> >
> > If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.
> >
> > I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
> >
> > system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
> >
> > I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
> >
> > I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
> >
> > I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
> >
> > However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
> >
> > Error in .local(drv, ...) :
> >   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
> >
> > Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
> >
> > If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
> >
> > I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
> >
> >
> >
> >

Christine

messages.subject: Meager locale choices on shinyapp.io
messages.body_plain:
The R sort() function makes use of the locale settings to determine how to do string comparisons. According to:

print(system("locale -a", intern = TRUE))

the only available locales on the shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io> servers are:

[1] "C"  "C.UTF-8"  "POSIX"
This means that characters string sorting doesn't work as expected (i.e. ordering is ASCII-betical, rather than alphabetical). For proper alphabetical string sorting, a local like "en_US.UTF-8" is needed.

So, two questions:

- Why aren't more locales available on the shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io> servers?

- Are there other sorting methods that don't rely on locale settings?

Thanks,
Eric

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] 100MB file limit for uploads
messages.body_plain:
Hi Boris,
Unfortunately the change to support larger uploads wasn't quite as simple as I was hoping it would be.  I spent a little time with this and tested out a download from dropbox for a file that is publicly viewable.  Here is what I did using a package called downloader:

Within global.R  (or before your shinyServer function ) you would have logic that looks something like this:

library(downloader)

URL <- "https://......"
download(URL, destfile = "./filename")

If you wanted to make it a little smarter, you could check to see if the file is there and not bother downloading it if it has already been downloaded. (file.exists , and file.info <http://file.info> would be what I would look at)

We will come up with a more elegant solution for folks.  Please let me know if this works for you.
-
Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: API best practice
messages.body_plain:
Hi Josh,
Apologies for the delay, I forgot to close the loop after I got the response. There is no best practice today that we would recommend, putting the API key in the server.R file is just as secure as trying to put it in some other file within the application.   There may be techniques that make it so that you don't ever store the key on disk anywhere, for example you make a call out to a service on your side at application startup over SSL and that end point is locked down so it would only respond to calls from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. As you know none of these solutions are completely bulletproof unfortunately, but that could be a marginally better way to handle that.  We have batted around the idea of HSMs, but we aren't convinced that the overhead and complexity really buys you as much.  We are of course open to other suggestions if you have them.

As for adding users, it is absolutely our intention to provide such an api in the shinyapps package.  We have prioritized a few items like support for private github repos, improved support for various locales, making it easier for folks to see their billing cycle information, improving invoices, renaming accounts and finally support for application deletes.  Adding/removing users programmatically is at the top of the very next batch of work.

-Tareef

anti-aliasing, and it is just that it does not work well for certain
point symbols, such as the (unfortunate?) default point shape (solid
point without border) in ggplot2. More info here:
http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/png-type-cairo-point-symbols-without-boarders-are-not-anti-aliased-td4678745.html

So you may either use Cairo, or change the point shape in your plot.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shiny r questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Subhash,
We tried to capture answers to those between our product page (http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/) and our FAQ for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> (http://www.rstudio.com/resources/faqs/)  but clearly we need to do a bit more.  I would appreciate knowing if you had a chance to read over the content on the website and if you have any suggestions on how we can make things easier for new users.

Here are the answers with a little more color that we will probably fold back into the FAQ.

Active Hours : Hours that your application is not idle.  It is measured on a minute by minute basis.  An application will typically be up when it is either servicing the request of a user, or it is within the timeout period after the last user's session ended.

5 Applications: means 5 active applications in your account.  Ie.  they are either "Active" or "Sleeping" in your account.  Archived applications don't count against your 5 application.

Old applications can be archived today.  We will add support for deletion in the coming weeks.

What are instances:  I would encourage you to read this doc http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps-io-performance-tuning/ to give you a sense for what that is.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Tareef

messages.body_plain:
We are happy to announce several improvements to the shinyapps.io <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/> platform.

Using private packages on github.com <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/204536558-Enabling-use-of-private-packages-on-github-com> -- for customers who have developed their own proprietary private R packages, you can now use those packages in the shiny applications you deploy to shinyapps.io <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/>

Download your application <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/204536588-Downloading-your-application-from-shinyapps-io> -- Have you ever misplaced your application on your local machine?  You can now download the version of your app that is running on shinyapps.io <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/>.

Finally we made a few tweaks to the dashboard and invoices to give you better visibility into your billing cycle information, and to make it a bit easier for you to expense your subscription internally.

As always, please don't hesitate to send us your feedback.

Best,

The shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> team

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I did get this to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, with help from Tareef and Chad. They were going to write up the process. However, in short:

1. Create a set of SSH keys on your local machine

2. Add the relevant key to your database server. I used ssh-copy-id for this. There are many tutorials online. I use Digital Ocean and this is a good start: https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-configure-ssh-key-based-authentication-on-a-linux-server

3. Upload both public and private SSH key into a directory accessible from your Shiny app. I initially had some reservations about uploading the private key, but after thinking about it the alternative is an SSH tunnel initiated through username/password which is just as insecure, maybe more. Effectively your Shiny app server needs the private key because it's really taking the place of your local machine when making the SSH tunnel.

4. Then I have the following code (change credentials as appropriate):

# Load db connector library

library("RMySQL")

# Change permissions on SSH keys

system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa.pub"))
system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa"))

# Open SSH connection

system(paste("ssh -v -f -N -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -i /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa -L 3306:localhost:3306 user@hostname sleep 20"))

# Database query

con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host='127.0.0.1', user='youDBUser', password='yourDBPassword', dbname='yourDBName')

sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM database.tablename", sep="")

queryResults <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)

dbDisconnect(con)

Key things to remember here are the path to the SSH key, make sure the directory where the SSH keys are located is writable and your user has rights to change the permissions, make sure port 3306 is open on both machines.

I think that's it. It took me a few attempts, with some rookie errors, but with Tareef and Chad's help we found success.

Good luck.

Cheers
Phill

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Phil!

I need to digest this some. I have shinyapps.i.o, but was also experimenting with Amazon.

So, I think I may have Amazon issues. I set the database up there and a separate server. Right now I can do everything I want on just the server. But everyone is talking about these SHH tunnels... My understanding is the classic architecture is to get the web app to talk to the database, user access through the web app.

Is using MySQL on the same server that the app is running the same thing, or do I need to set up a separate database (as kinda a best practice?)

I was able to connect to MySQL on Amazon server, but key was to create a user and grant privileges. I used the key to set that up, but from my pc's command line(Putty). Once it was set up, in my app I can just use RMySQL without specifying any keys. I could never do the same on Amazon RDS instance - creating a user with the same privileges there. I think if I could I could just use that address, user, and password in my RMySQL call.

The link is extremely helpful and I was unaware of the system() function in R. Thanks so much for the reply, gives me options and paths to follow.

Cheers
Mike

Sent from my iPad

On Mar 30, 2015, at 10:46 AM, Phill Clarke <phill...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Mike,
>
> I did get this to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, with help from Tareef and Chad. They were going to write up the process. However, in short:
>
> 1. Create a set of SSH keys on your local machine
>
> 2. Add the relevant key to your database server. I used ssh-copy-id for this. There are many tutorials online. I use Digital Ocean and this is a good start: https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-configure-ssh-key-based-authentication-on-a-linux-server
>
> 3. Upload both public and private SSH key into a directory accessible from your Shiny app. I initially had some reservations about uploading the private key, but after thinking about it the alternative is an SSH tunnel initiated through username/password which is just as insecure, maybe more. Effectively your Shiny app server needs the private key because it's really taking the place of your local machine when making the SSH tunnel.
>
> 4. Then I have the following code (change credentials as appropriate):
>
> # Load db connector library
>
> library("RMySQL")
>
> # Change permissions on SSH keys
>
> system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa.pub"))
> system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa"))
>
> # Open SSH connection
>
> system(paste("ssh -v -f -N -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -i /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa -L 3306:localhost:3306 user@hostname sleep 20"))
>
> # Database query
>
> con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host='127.0.0.1', user='youDBUser', password='yourDBPassword', dbname='yourDBName')
>
> sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM database.tablename", sep="")
>
> queryResults <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
>
> dbDisconnect(con)
>
> Key things to remember here are the path to the SSH key, make sure the directory where the SSH keys are located is writable and your user has rights to change the permissions, make sure port 3306 is open on both machines.
>
> I think that's it. It took me a few attempts, with some rookie errors, but with Tareef and Chad's help we found success.
>
> Good luck.
>
> Cheers
> Phill
>
>
>

> > Can I get in on this? I want to do something similar. I have gotten part way...

> > I was able to put my shiny app on an amazon EC2 server and set up MySQL on that server. It works great. I can change the data on the data base from the app using RMySQL based on user interaction on the app.

> > > > > > I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Error in .local(drv, ...) :
> > > > > >   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
